changes.why: Calque of 'far to me': Turkish uzak governs the ablative (TDK sozluk.gov.tr, entry uzak: 'O böyle işlerden pek uzaktır'). 'Benden ne kadar uzak?' is the case Turkish takes; ar كم يبعد عني is the same ablative sense.

changes.before: Hikâyesi olan bir vaha. Bahçeleri ve hurmalıkları arasında dolaşın.
changes.after: Hikâyesi olan bir vaha. Bahçeleri ve hurma ağaçları arasında dolaşın.
changes.why: Fence: 'hurmalık' means a date grove, a different thing from 'palms' (the source and ar النخيل say palms); orchards and groves would be near-duplicates. 'hurma ağaçları' is the form already published in the TM ('hurma ağaçlarıyla dolu').

changes.before: Mağaralarla dolu bir dağdan Arap Körfezi kıyısındaki bir limana kadar — bir kategori seçin ve keşfe başlayın.
changes.after: Mağaralarla dolu bir dağdan Arap Körfezi'ndeki bir limana kadar — bir kategori seçin ve keşfe başlayın.
changes.why: Fence: 'kıyısındaki' (on the shore of) states a position the source does not (en 'a port on the Arabian Gulf'). The locative 'Körfezi'ndeki' is what the source says; the suffix follows the termbase entry (Arap Körfezi'nde, vowel i).

'yapı' means a built structure and narrows 'sites' (en 'religious sites', ar المواقع الدينية); 'mekân' (TDK sozluk.gov.tr, entry mekân: 'bulunulan yer') is the word already used in this batch for 'place' (det.fromPlace, search.placeholder). Spelling kept with the circumflex per the batch decision.

checks.finding: Entry 'çevrim içi' (two words) exists, noun, informatics, with compounds 'çevrim içi eğitim' and 'çevrim içi öğrenme'; 'çevrimiçi' (one word) has no entry. So the two-word form the batch uses is the TDK form.
Article spells it as one word 'çevrimiçi' (opposite 'çevrimdışı'); it does not mention 'çevrim içi'. Wikipedia and TDK disagree; TDK is the spelling authority in the pipeline, so two words stays.

checks.query_or_url: web search: "çevrim içi mağaza" OR "online mağaza" OR "internet mağazaları"
checks.finding: Result titles/snippets: odoo.com/tr_TR 'Çevrim içi mağazanızı oluşturun'; shopify.com/tr/blog 'cevrimici magaza nasil acilir' (URL slug only); godaddy.com/tr-tr help 'Web siteme online mağaza bölümü ekleme'. Both 'çevrim içi mağaza' and 'online mağaza' are in use in Turkish product pages; neither is an error. No page was opened, only the search summary was read.

Footer 'İletişim' (under HAKKINDA) and 'Kullanım Koşulları'; a category tile 'Gezilecek Yerler'. Confirms foot.l.contact 'İletişim' and the term 'gezilecek yerler' for attractions on the official Ministry portal. No 'Gizlilik' label there (only 'KVKK Aydınlatma Metni'). No skip-link or home-page label was visible in the fetched text.

Page is English ('Plan Your Trip', 'Privacy Policy', 'Cookie Policy'); the /tr page keeps 'Plan Your Trip' in English, uses 'Türkiye destinasyonları' as a heading, 'Çerez Politikası' and 'KVKK Aydınlatma Metni' in the footer. It supplies no Turkish wording for 'plan your trip' or 'contact', so it neither confirms nor contradicts 'Gezinizi planlayın'. Note the site itself uses 'destinasyon', which the batch style rules ban for our text.

checks.query_or_url: web search: "Gizlilik Politikası" "Kullanım Koşulları" ... "Politikalar ve Koşullar"
checks.finding: No source found using 'Politikalar ve Koşullar' as a footer label (the search tool itself said it could not confirm the label as standard). Canva's Turkish legal page lists 'Gizlilik Politikası' and 'Kullanım Koşulları' as separate items. Result: the label is grammatical and literal to en/ar, but not attested as a Turkish footer convention.

'yeme içme' (two words, no hyphen) is a TDK entry: 'Türlü yiyecek ve içeceklerle beslenme'. nav.dining spelling confirmed; the sense is eating and drinking, fine as a section label for restaurants and cafés.

Entry uzak; example 'O böyle işlerden pek uzaktır' shows the ablative complement. Basis for det.distance. The page has no 'benden uzak' example, so the ablative is attested for uzak in general, not for this exact phrase.
Entry 'mekân' with the circumflex; sense 1 'Bulunulan yer', sense 2 a place set apart for an activity. Confirms spelling (batch circumflex decision) and the sense 'place'.
Not read: the first four returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, the airline page timed out. No claim about their wording is made.

fence_removed.why: the source says 'on the Arabian Gulf', not on its shore
source says palms; a grove is a different, stronger claim; replaced by 'hurma ağaçları'

notes: Scope: 95 interface strings, no body text. Most controls were checked against the register of the TDK dictionary and the one official Turkish portal that loaded (kulturportali.gov.tr); the large e-commerce and travel sites blocked the fetch tool (HTTP 403), so no claim rests on them.

OPEN QUESTION nav.stores (header label): 'Çevrim içi mağazalar' is kept. Evidence: two-word form is the TDK headword; 'çevrim içi mağaza' is used on Odoo's Turkish page (search snippet); the one-word 'çevrimiçi' is Wikipedia's spelling but has no TDK entry; 'online mağazalar' also appears (GoDaddy TR snippet) but is a loan the termbase has not decided. Alternative 'Mağazalar' alone reads as physical shops (ar says only المتاجر). The decision between kept and shortened belongs to the measure-header-fit run (20 characters, longest of the nine); nothing here shortens it because no source settles it and the measure has not run. Raised to stage 7 / owner as the only genuinely open string.

OPEN QUESTION foot.l.privacy: 'Politikalar ve koşullar' kept literal to en and ar. It is grammatical, but I found no Turkish site using it (search tool reported none; the portal that loaded uses 'Kullanım Koşulları'; Turkish sites typically split 'Gizlilik Politikası' and 'Kullanım Koşulları'). Narrowing to 'Gizlilik ve kullanım koşulları' would claim a content (privacy) the English does not state, and I do not know what the linked page contains, so I did not do it. To settle: look at what the target page holds, then decide; if it is privacy plus terms, 'Gizlilik ve kullanım koşulları' is the more natural Turkish label.

Kept without change after comparison: nav.attractions and the others using 'gezilecek yerler' (the portal tile 'Gezilecek Yerler' confirms the term); foot.l.contact 'İletişim' (portal footer); Yeme içme / Restoranlar ve kafeler pair (header/footer lengths, TDK entry); 'Ana sayfa', 'Gezinti yolu', 'İçeriğe geçin' (standard UI terms, not contradicted by anything read; the large sites that would show them did not load); det.* strings that are TM-approved pairs are untouched (binding).

Considered and left: foot.col.site 'Site' (a bare 'site' also means a housing estate in Turkish; the column sits next to Discover and Plan, so the sense is clear; 'Web sitesi' is the fallback if a reader flags it). lang.suggest.text 'Bu sayfanın Türkçesi de var' keeps the 'de' (also) of 'is available in Turkish'; wiring issue stays in source_defects. nav.dining 'Yeme içme' omits the cafés that the English names; it is the deliberate short header form and the full pair is in nav.dine.
No -mektedir/bulunmaktadır chains, stacked olan, or 'bu' for every 'the' remain; the only 'bu' is in fav.add ('Bu yeri kaydedin' for 'Save this place'), which is a real demonstrative.
Gulf: the only occurrence is list.lead, 'Arap Körfezi' (P5), now with the locative 'Arap Körfezi'ndeki' per the termbase suffix vowel.

source_defects.defect: ar has an extra clause not in en ('من الأماكن التراثية في الأحساء إلى متاحف الأحساء'); en is the translation source, the Turkish follows en.

The suggest-bar strings are written from the viewpoint of the page being offered ('available in <this language>'); on a Turkish frame they only make sense if a Turkish counterpart of a non-Turkish page exists. Not a text defect; flagged for wiring.
